frames.narration: The agent on host web-17 sends a point for the series cpu_usage{host=web-17, region=eu}: 61.5 at 12:00:15. The router hashes the metric name and labels together and gets shard 2, so every point of this series will go to the same machine.

Shard 2 first appends the point to its write-ahead log, a sequential write, and then to the open chunk of the series in the head block. The series already exists, with id 4711, so the labels are not stored again.

The point is compressed as it joins the chunk. The time is exactly 15 seconds after the previous one, as before, so the delta-of-delta is zero and takes 1 bit. The previous value was 61.25, and the XOR of the two differs in just 2 bits, so a new window of meaningful bits is written: 2 + 5 + 6 + 2 = 15 bits. With the 1 bit for the time that makes 16 bits, 2 bytes, where an uncompressed point takes 16 bytes. A value that repeats takes a single bit.
The shard sends the log record to its replica and acknowledges the write once the replica has it. If the shard dies now, the replica holds the point.

Later the head is full: it holds two hours of points. It is written out as an immutable block together with its index, which lists, for each label pair such as region=eu, the sorted ids of the series that have it. The log segments for those two hours can now be deleted.
A dashboard asks for the average cpu_usage per region for the last 6 hours, filtered by region=eu. The query engine asks shard 2 for the series that have the name cpu_usage and region=eu.

Intersecting two sorted lists gives 1,240 series out of 2.1 million on the shard. Only the 2 blocks that overlap the last 6 hours beyond the head, plus the head itself, are opened, and only the chunks of those 1,240 series are decoded. The shard returns a partial sum and count, not the points.

The query engine adds the sums and counts from every shard and divides, and the dashboard draws the line. A month later the compactor will roll these points into 5-minute min, max, sum and count, and the raw points will be deleted after their retention period.
